_comment: THE ONE PLACE the plugin's identity lives. Everything that carries it — .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json the 92 permission rules in skills/soc-investigate/settings.snippet.json and the identity.sh include that install.sh/preflight.sh source — is GENERATED from this file by gen_identity.py; CI fails if they drift. To re-brand or re-key the plugin (e.g. a vendor catalog shipping it under its own name), change `name`/`displayName`/`description` here and run `python3 plugin/gen_identity.py`. The optional `distribution` block holds everything that is per-COPY rather than per-plugin, and it has two halves that do different things. The terms half (`license`, `homepage`, `repository`, plus the prose keys `vendor`, `terms`, `support`) says this copy is redistributed under someone else's terms: the manifests take those values and the marked community-only/distribution-only prose switches. The listing half (`icon`, `documentationUrl`, `supportUrl`, `privacyPolicyUrl`, `termsOfServiceUrl`) only describes a directory ENTRY, is emitted into the Claude manifest alone, and does NOT switch the prose — so this repo can carry its own listing without its docs calling it a redistribution. `icon` is a path to an image shipped in the payload; the four URLs must be https:// with a host. The top-level `license` stays the software's either way and keeps driving the SPDX headers, README badge and identity.sh. `name` is load-bearing: it is the Claude Code plugin key and the skill/MCP namespace prefix (`<name>:<skill>`, `mcp__plugin_<name>_<server>__<tool>`) that the permission gate matches on. `mcpServer` must equal permissions.json's `server` and the server key in .mcp.json/.mcp.codex.json; the generator refuses to run when they disagree.
name: raffkin
shortDescription: Triage Exabeam New-Scale alerts and cases end to end — evidence, verdict, and a guarded write path.
description: Raffkin — agentic SOC analyst skill suite. Investigates and triages Exabeam New-Scale alerts and cases through the Exabeam MCP: evidence gathering, entity pivots, threat/false-positive verdict, and action — with containment recommended for human approval and dismiss/close gated by the host agent's tool-approval rules.
